summary: SIL1 reject-storm alarm. Re-derived every load-bearing claim rather than accepting codex-2's summary. Three counters are genuinely distinct, not one aliased with a lower bound: _v2_exit_close_failures (consecutive, reset by HELD, the unreachable one), the NEW _v2_exit_reject_alarm_count (service.py:612), and _v2_exit_reject_total (per acct+symbol episode total, cleared only by real progress). _V2_EXIT_MAX_REJECTS_PER_EPISODE is UNCHANGED at 20 (service.py:448) — the alarm does not lower the ceiling, which was the specific outcome the operator's decouple decision exists to prevent, since the ceiling's failure mode is abandoning a live exit twelve rejects early while the alarm's is a false page. _V2_EXIT_REJECT_ALARM_THRESHOLD_SCHWAB = 8 at :455. The threshold function at :4703 returns the constant ONLY when the account equals the configured Schwab account and returns None for every other account, with the uncovered rationale in the code at :449-454 including the line that Webull coverage must not be inferred from SIL1 existing — live:orb is explicitly UNSET because its scoped benign band reaches 19 across 80 episodes, confirmed after restricting to the same population as the Schwab distribution, so no threshold below 20 is defensible. The alarm is keyed on the rejected-event path beside [OMS-V2-EXIT-REJECT-CEILING], never on broker reject wording, which matters because the verbatim refusal string appears zero times in every retained log file and exists only in broker_orders.payload reject_reason; a reason-keyed alarm would also have been Schwab-only, the exact defect CONF3 exists to fix. Safety ordering verified by reading: the alarm publishes AFTER session.commit() and outside the try, so an alert-write failure cannot alter or roll back the broker result. Operator requirement (e) — the symbol visible on screen while exits are stood down, not merely paged — is met in control_plane.py, which orders non-closed oms-risk SIL1 incidents to sort priority 0 so the affected symbol cannot be pushed off the ten-row dashboard by newer unrelated incidents. INDEPENDENT MUTATION, not codex's: forcing _v2_exit_reject_alarm_threshold to return the Schwab constant for every account turned test_sil1_leaves_live_orb_explicitly_unalarmed RED (1 failed / 90 passed); restoring gave 91 passed. The explicitly-uncovered decision is therefore pinned by a control that can come out false. validate PASS on both runs. NOT COVERED BY THIS PIN, recorded so it is not inherited: PR #902 modifies the same file from the same base and CONFLICTS with this one on trial merge (both insert at original service.py lines 307 and 5109), so whichever merges second must rebase and be re-verified and re-pinned against the new base; this record covers only PR #903 at this exact head.
